regime.headline: Risk-on
regime.paragraph: Investors added risk across equities and credit: US Treasury yields 2Y -1bp to 4.68% and 10Y unch to 5.00%. The US curve saw a bull steepener in 2s10s (+1bp to 32bp). The dollar rose 0.2%, gold fell 0.5%, the S&P 500 rose 0.7% and Brent fell 4.1%. US high-yield spreads tightened 2bp. The standout move was UK 2Y Gilt (+22bp, 6.1x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries were little changed, 2Y -1bp to 4.68% and 10Y unch to 5.00%: a bull steepener (2s10s +1bp). Markets removed 18bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +70bp). The dollar rose 0.2% and the S&P 500 rose 0.7%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +22bp to 4.93% and 10Y unch to 5.34%: a twist flattener (2s10s -23bp). BoE pricing was steady at +113bp over 12 months. Sterling fell 0.4% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.7%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds sold off with the front end leading, 2Y +6bp to 3.08% and 10Y +4bp to 3.43%: a bear flattener (2s10s -2bp). BTP-Bund tightened 12bp to 107bp. ECB pricing was steady at +67bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The euro fell 0.5% and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 0.8%.

relationships.statement: Tighter BTP–Bund spreads signalled stronger demand for periphery risk.
relationships.lesson: BTP–Bund is the euro area's main gauge of sovereign and fragmentation risk; it usually widens with risk-off and narrows when risk appetite is strong.

relationships.statement: EUR/USD fell even as the Treasury–Bund spread narrowed.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: A wider US–Japan yield gap lifted USD/JPY.
relationships.lesson: USD/JPY is one of the FX pairs most tightly linked to rate differentials, because the yen is a funding currency for carry trades.

relationships.statement: Lower oil pulled US breakevens down.
relationships.lesson: Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Gilts outperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific relief from data, BoE pricing or fiscal news.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.
Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

interview.question: Why did the UK 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The UK 2Y moved +22bp and the 10Y unch, so 2s10s moved -23bp to 41bp: a twist flattener. Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 10% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.8 hikes (70bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.72%. The 12-month pricing moved -18bp on the day. Method: Fed funds futures (CME FedWatch method). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +70bp is 2.8 moves.

interview.question: Why did BTP–Bund spreads tighten?
interview.answer: BTP–Bund moved -12bp to 107bp. The spread prices Italian sovereign credit and redenomination risk relative to Germany. It widens with global risk-off, Italian fiscal or political news, or a hawkish ECB (higher rates raise debt-servicing concerns), and tightens with strong risk appetite and carry demand. The ECB's TPI backstop limits disorderly widening. Today's Euro Stoxx move was +0.8%.

interview.question: Why did Gilts outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved unch versus +4bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -4bp to 191bp (93th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did JGBs outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y JGBs moved -4bp versus +4bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -4bp to -65bp (46th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.
